guide.title: Two endpoints that look alike and are not
guide.subtitle: Receipts and replies arrive at separate URLs
guide.excerpt: Delivery receipts and inbound replies are different endpoints, configured in different places in your provider’s console. Configure only the receipt URL and opt-out handling stops — silently, with no error anywhere.

p: Outbound outcomes arrive at the receipt URL. Replies from recipients — including STOP — arrive at the inbound URL. They are separate paths and, in most provider consoles, separate configuration screens under different headings.

This is the single most common way to lose opt-out handling. Receipts keep working, the message log looks healthy, and the suppression list simply never receives any entries. Nothing reports a fault, because from the provider’s point of view nothing is wrong.

sections.h: What the token proves, and what it does not
p: The token in the URL identifies which account the event belongs to. It does not prove that the event genuinely came from the provider — per-provider signature verification is not implemented. Treat the inbound endpoint as authenticated by obscurity of the token, and treat provider signatures as something to verify yourself if your risk model needs it.

sections.h: Not every provider sends STOP to you
list: Some providers handle opt-out at the carrier level, in which case no inbound event is produced at all and the platform never sees the reply.
Where that happens, your own suppression record is a reconciliation tool rather than the only line of defense.
The provider identifier in the path is case-insensitive, so a differently-cased value is not a configuration bug.
sections.scope: Inbound handling and suppression are implemented for the SMS channel. Email and WhatsApp do not carry them today.
